document_check.note: Deng et al., 'Novel methodology for detection and prediction of mild cognitive impairment using resting-state EEG', Alzheimer's & Dementia 2024;20:145-158 (accepted July 2023, doi:10.1002/alz.13411). 137 Black American participants (84 HC, 53 MCI); the classifier uses only time-varying functional-connectivity features, as the review states.

cited_result: Discrimination of MCI from HC by a weighted-majority-vote ensemble of 21 AdaBoost classifiers built on multiscale time-varying EEG functional-connectivity features, with no spectral-power features: leave-one-out accuracy 91.97% and 3-fold accuracy 91.17%.
tool_reason: The cited result is the classification performance of a machine-learning model built on many EEG connectivity features.

domains.rationale: A community sample of older adults with self-reported cognitive concern, all diagnosed by consensus, is an appropriate cross-sectional source, but no exclusion criteria are reported.

signalling.question: Were appropriate data sources used?
signalling.quote: persons were recruited if they considered themselves to be fully functioning, though they also responded positively to a question asking if they were concerned that they may have experienced a potential decline in cognitive ability over the past year.

signalling.question: Were all inclusions and exclusions of participants appropriate?
signalling.quote: Searched for exclusion criteria (neurological or psychiatric disease, medication, EEG quality exclusions); none reported. Recruitment text: "We recruited 137 community-dwelling Black participants (122 females, 15 males), ranging in age from 60 to 90 years, from the greater Detroit area."

domains.rationale: The same EEG system and protocol were used for everyone; features are computed algorithmically from a 3-minute resting recording available at the point of use; manual artefact inspection is not reported as blinded, but artefact rejection is unlikely to be driven by diagnosis.

signalling.question: Were predictors defined and assessed in a similar way for all participants?
signalling.quote: We performed EEG recordings in a community center at the University of Michigan (UM) Detroit Center or the Institute of Gerontology at Wayne State University using the same EEG system.

signalling.question: Were predictor assessments made without knowledge of outcome data?
signalling.quote: Off-line inspection was used to identify and remove segments of EEG contaminating either excessive noise, saturation, or lack of EEG activity. ... An automatic computerized procedure using a rejection criterion of +/– 100 mV on any channel affected by artifacts (muscular, instrumental) was used to identify acceptable epochs.

signalling.question: Are all predictors available at the time the model is intended to be used?
signalling.quote: each participant received a 3-minute, eye-closed resting-state EEG recording.

domains.rationale: Consensus diagnosis with the NACC UDS is a standard, appropriate outcome, but the interval between EEG and the diagnosis used as label is not reported, and Table 2 shows diagnoses up to a year earlier than the EEG for some participants.

signalling.question: Was the outcome determined appropriately?
signalling.quote: were diagnosed through the MADRC consensus conference using the National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center (NACC) Uniform Data Set (UDS)—84 of them being HC and 53 with MCI

signalling.question: Was a pre-specified or standard outcome definition used?
signalling.quote: National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center (NACC) Uniform Data Set (UDS)

signalling.question: Were predictors excluded from the outcome definition?
signalling.quote: were diagnosed through the MADRC consensus conference using the National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center (NACC) Uniform Data Set (UDS) (no indication that EEG entered the consensus)

signalling.question: Was the outcome defined and determined in a similar way for all participants?
signalling.quote: All participants ... were diagnosed through the MADRC consensus conference

signalling.question: Was the outcome determined without knowledge of predictor information?
signalling.quote: No statement on blinding; the connectivity features are research-derived and not part of the UDS consensus process ("were diagnosed through the MADRC consensus conference using the National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center (NACC) Uniform Data Set (UDS)").

signalling.question: Was the time interval between predictor assessment and outcome determination appropriate?
signalling.quote: Searched for the EEG-to-baseline-diagnosis interval; not reported. Table 2, subject 10: "2016" | "MCI, −0.5019" | "2015, aMCI" (EEG test year 2016, first-visit diagnosis 2015).

domains.rationale: Very few events per candidate feature (53 MCI against 198 primitive features per window size across 8 window sizes). Features were screened by univariable t-tests on all 137 participants before cross-validation (leakage), and the 21 voters were chosen by their leave-one-out accuracy and then evaluated with the same cross-validation (test data used for tuning). Only accuracy is reported (no AUC, no calibration), class imbalance was not handled, and there is no external validation.

signalling.question: Were there a reasonable number of participants with the outcome?
signalling.quote: Here L = 25, 50, 100, 200, 400, 800, 1600, and 3200, and M = 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, or 45. (with 198 primitive features per window size and 53 MCI participants)

signalling.question: Were continuous and categorical predictors handled appropriately?
signalling.quote: Using a regularized LDA (linear discriminant analysis), we mapped the feature vector of each participant to a point in a one-dimensional subspace or axis

signalling.question: Were all enrolled participants included in the analysis?
signalling.quote: the shortest length of the eye-closed, resting-state EEG among all the 137 participants was 110 s. Therefore, for each participant, we kept the first 110 s

signalling.question: Were participants with missing data handled appropriately?
signalling.quote: for each participant, we kept the first 110 s of the eye-closed, resting-state EEG signals of all the 64 channels for further analysis. (no missing data reported)

signalling.question: Was selection of predictors based on univariable analysis avoided?
signalling.quote: each primitive feature for all the 137 subjects was put together and screened using the t test, and only M out of the 198 primitive features with the smallest P-values were selected to formulate the feature vector.

signalling.question: Were complexities in the data (including class imbalance) accounted for appropriately?
signalling.quote: First, we have more HC (84) than MCI (53). As a result, the model is better trained for HC. We can see that in all the cross-validation tests, the model achieves a higher accuracy in the discrimination of HC than that of the MCI.

signalling.question: Were relevant model performance measures evaluated appropriately?
signalling.quote: The leave-one-out cross-validation accuracy is 91.97% and 3-fold accuracy is 91.17%.

signalling.question: Were model overfitting, underfitting and optimism in model performance accounted for? (split at participant level; preprocessing, selection and tuning within training folds; test set held out)
signalling.quote: We selected N = 21 classifiers, which delivered the highest accuracy in leave-one-out cross-validation as our voters, as marked by the red boxes in Figure 3. The same group of voters was used for the soft discrimination of HC and MCI for leave-one-out, 10-fold, 5-fold, and 3-fold cross-validations

signalling.question: Do predictors and their assigned weights in the final model correspond to the results from the reported multivariable analysis?
signalling.quote: Searched for a final fitted model or weights; only selected-feature tables in the supplement are referenced ("The complete tables of selected features ... can be found in the Supplemental File").

overall: High risk of bias (PROBAST: analysis domain high; participants and outcome unclear; predictors low; internally validated only)
overall_rationale: The analysis domain is high on its own. Univariable feature screening on the full data set and choosing classifiers by the same cross-validated accuracy that is then reported mean the 91.97% figure is optimistic apparent performance, not a validated estimate. The events-per-feature ratio is extremely low and there is no external validation.

applicability.rationale: Community-dwelling Black American older adults, about 89% female, all reporting cognitive concern; applicability to other MCI populations is uncertain.
